title: Replace shell CI entrypoint with Go binary; add dependency rollback safeguard and branch green check
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: our current .github/workflows entrypoints are heavy shell scripts that are a source of flakiness (env handling, quoting, platform differences) and make it hard to add cross-cutting safeguards like automatic dependency rollback when a dependency upgrade causes regressions. This PR replaces the fragile shell entrypoint with a small statically linked Go binary (ci-entrypoint) and adds two safety features: 1) dep-rollback-safeguard: an opt-in post-merge monitor that opens an automated revert PR when a single-commit dependency bump correlates with test/regression signals; 2) green-branch-safeguard: a pre-merge gate that requires a recent green run on the target branch within the last N minutes before allowing merge (protects against merging into a corrupted main). Scope: refactor CI entrypoint, add tooling under tools/ci, introduce a lightweight manifest-prune helper to remove stale devDeps, wire up telemetry for CI entrypoint and rollback events. Checklist: - [x] Implement Go entrypoint and replace shell logic - [x] Add dep-rollback controller and unit tests - [x] Hook green-branch-safeguard into the merge bot (merge queue) - [x] Add manifest-prune script and integration smoke test - [x] Metrics and tracing hooks for critical paths - [x] Docs: update CONTRIBUTING.md with new dev CI flow Rolling blockers & related: references ENG-7789 (CI robustness) and ENG-7810 (dependency incident hardening). This PR intentionally keeps the runtime of the Go binary minimal (no remote calls except optional telemetry) and defers aggressive heuristics for rollback to a future tuning PR. Linear/Jira: SUP-1426 was the customer incident that motivated automatic rollback for dependency bumps.

release_notes:
- Replaced shell-based CI entrypoint with a small Go binary to reduce flakiness and improve observability.
- Added an opt-in dependency rollback safeguard that can open an automated revert PR when a single-commit dependency bump causes test regressions.
- Introduced green-branch-safeguard to require a recently green target branch before merging.
- Added manifest-prune helper to proactively prune unused devDependencies.

notes_for_release_engineering: No blocking changes to release process; merge-bot config updated to enforce green-branch-safeguard. Release engineers should be aware that new telemetry tags exist (ci.entrypoint.* and ci.rollback.*) and can be used for incident triage.
why_this_is_unique: Instead of incremental script cleanup, this PR introduces a compiled entrypoint plus an automated safety mechanism (rollback controller) that actively mitigates dependency-caused regressions. The combination of a small binary for stability and a conservative rollback controller is a different approach from the prior pattern of purely policy-driven merge gates.
